solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Beauty in bed, attractive, getting stuck in to porridge?

indicators.note: something stuck into another thing ends up lodged inside it, so one word sits within the other

parts.note: brose is a Scottish oatmeal porridge
lush is informal for attractive or sexy

explanation.surface: A lovely woman in bed, tempting, tucks into her breakfast porridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beauty in bed' reads as a person between the sheets, but the bed is a flowerbed and the beauty is a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A blush rose is a pale pink garden rose variety, a beautiful flower growing in a flowerbed.

clue.text: One of spiritual purity, guy I had seen idly taking in satellite telly

parts.note: bo is American slang for a pal or fellow

indicators.note: to take in is to enclose or admit, so the jumbled letters wrap around the rest
something viewed idly is taken in loosely and carelessly, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written, ready for jumbling
a common short form of satellite
telly is British informal for television

explanation.surface: A spiritual man admits that a bloke watched satellite TV lazily.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the letters of 'I had' are jumbled; the satellite telly pieces sit inside that jumble, after the guy.
explanation.definitionFit: A bodhisattva in Buddhism is an enlightened being who delays nirvana to help others, a figure of spiritual purity.

clue.text: Bag some birds for a bit of fun

definitions.meaning: first meaning: as a verb, to catch skylarks
second meaning: a prank or frolic

explanation.surface: Shooting a few birds just for the sport of it.
explanation.walkthrough: Chambers lists the verb sense 'to catch larks', which is what 'bag some birds' describes.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means hunting skylarks; as a noun it means a playful escapade.

clue.text: Shelter king surrounded by flattery (not a queen?)

indicators.note: being surrounded means sitting inside another word, enclosed on both sides
not tells us to strip the named letters out of the word before using it

parts.note: sweet talk; sugar as flattery
A taken as written plus R for Regina, the queen
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A king hides away, cocooned in flattery, with no queen present.
explanation.walkthrough: SUG(ar) loses A and R, then K goes inside it. Skug is a Scots word, found in Chambers.
explanation.definitionFit: Skug is a Scots dialect noun and verb for shade, refuge or protection from the weather.

clue.text: Greeting no gossip? It's part of Buddhism

parts.note: a casual hello
an old word for no
ana are collected anecdotes and table talk about a person

explanation.surface: A hello with no chatter attached, says a Buddhist.
explanation.walkthrough: ANA, a collection of sayings or anecdotes, is a crossword regular.
explanation.definitionFit: Hinayana, the 'lesser vehicle', is the name given to the early conservative schools of Buddhism.

clue.text: Place for soaking flax, right weird if it's dry inside

parts.note: R is the standard abbreviation for right

indicators.note: inside places the dry element within the weird word

parts.note: eery is a variant spelling of eerie
TT means teetotal, so dry in the sense of not drinking

explanation.surface: A flax-soaking site seems strange when it is bone dry inside.
explanation.walkthrough: R + E(TT)ERY. Dry in crosswords often means abstaining from alcohol, hence TT for teetotal.
explanation.definitionFit: Retting is soaking flax to loosen its fibres, and a rettery is the place where that is done.

clue.text: Bilge from rising political leader, American

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means reading from the bottom up, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: PM, the Prime Minister
US, the United States

explanation.surface: Rubbish talk heard from an up-and-coming American politician.
explanation.walkthrough: Bilge looks like nonsense talk, but here it is the dirty water in a ship's bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: A sump is a pit or well where waste liquid collects, like the bilge at the bottom of a ship's hull.

clue.text: Philosopher losing his heart to universal god

indicators.note: the thinker gives away his central letter to the newcomer, which takes its place

parts.note: the Greek philosopher
U is the film-rating abbreviation for universal

explanation.surface: A philosopher falls in love with a deity who belongs to everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of PLATO is the middle A, swapped for U.
explanation.definitionFit: Pluto is the Roman god of the underworld, counterpart of the Greek Hades.

clue.text: Old US coin? There's always one lurking among obsolete Indian ones

indicators.note: something lurking among others is tucked away in their midst, so it goes inside

parts.note: pice were small former Indian coins
ay is an old and Scots form of aye, meaning ever
'un is a dialect form of one

explanation.surface: Among some old Indian coins there's always an American one tucked away.
explanation.walkthrough: PIC(AY UN)E. 'Ones' in the surface means coins, so Indian coins host the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A picayune was a small Spanish or US coin of the old South, worth about five cents, hence the word for trivial.

clue.text: Fly circling a vessel

indicators.note: to circle something is to go all the way round it, so one part encloses the other

parts.note: a bot is the larva of a botfly, and botfly itself
taken as written

explanation.surface: An insect buzzing round and round a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: BO(A)T. Bot as a fly is a Chambers sense worth knowing.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat is a small vessel for travelling on water.

clue.text: Chafings of the skin from working stonier grit

indicators.note: working suggests material being kneaded and processed into a new form

parts.note: the eleven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Skin sores caused by working with gritty stone.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural of intertrigo, a medical term worth knowing.
explanation.definitionFit: Intertrigo is inflammation of skin folds caused by friction, so intertrigos are skin chafings.

clue.text: Compulsive boozer, not silent after first is polished off

indicators.note: polishing off the first means finishing off and removing the opening letter

parts.note: a talkie was an early film with sound, unlike a silent

explanation.surface: A heavy drinker, quiet no more once the first glass has been drained.
explanation.walkthrough: TALKIE loses T. 'Polished off' looks like drinking a glass, fitting the boozer.
explanation.definitionFit: Alkie is informal slang for an alcoholic, someone who drinks compulsively.

clue.text: Two strong males overlapping, raw material for future sovereigns?

indicators.note: where two things overlap they share a part, so one copy of the shared letter goes

parts.note: a bull and a lion, both powerful male animals

explanation.surface: Two muscular men overlap, the stuff that tomorrow's kings are made of.
explanation.walkthrough: BULL and LION share their L. Sovereigns are not monarchs but gold coins.
explanation.definitionFit: Bullion is gold or silver in bars, the raw metal from which sovereign coins are minted.

clue.text: Old-fashioned drawl produced by duke, a turn off

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for duke

indicators.note: off means gone bad or out of order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, ready for jumbling

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned drawl from a duke that puts people off.
explanation.walkthrough: Draunt is an obsolete Scots word in Chambers, a variant of drant.
explanation.definitionFit: To draunt is to drawl or drone, an archaic Scots word for a slow tedious way of speaking.

clue.text: Swine-fever giving wretched leper less energy, with discharge around

indicators.note: around means the discharge wraps on both sides of the jumble
wretched means in a sorry, battered state, so the remaining letters are jumbled
less means minus, so the named letter is taken away

parts.note: pus is matter discharged from a wound
taken as written
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A pig disease leaves a sickly leper drained of strength and oozing.
explanation.walkthrough: The energy comes off before the jumbling, and the discharge then wraps round the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Purples is an old name for swine fever, from the purple blotches on infected pigs, and also for purpura.

clue.text: Old coin one found in conduit

indicators.note: found in means located inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a duct is a channel or pipe
a, the indefinite article, means one

explanation.surface: An antique coin turns up lodged in a drainpipe.
explanation.walkthrough: DUC(A)T. One standing for A is a common crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: The ducat was a gold or silver coin used across Europe, especially in Venice, now historical.

clue.text: Finish up tucking into a drink? Good cheer

indicators.note: tucking into means pushing inside something, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a glass is a drink, as in 'a glass of wine'

indicators.note: in a down clue up means reading from the bottom upward, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: the end is the finish

explanation.surface: Finishing off a drink and tucking in brings good cheer.
explanation.walkthrough: GLA(DNE)SS. 'Tucking into' suggests eating, but it signals insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Gladness is joy or happiness, the feeling of being in good cheer.

clue.text: Rebellious phase away from the capital

parts.note: up as in 'up in arms', in revolt
a state or condition

explanation.surface: A rebellious stage in someone's life spent far from the big city.
explanation.walkthrough: Up as rebellious is the sense in 'the people are up'.
explanation.definitionFit: Upstate, in American usage, means the part of a state remote from its largest or capital city.

clue.text: It's hot in Lesotho, awfully — fire can go through it

indicators.note: in places one element within the country's name before jumbling
awfully suggests something done badly, so the combined letters are scrambled

parts.note: the African kingdom, taken as written
H is the tap abbreviation for hot

explanation.surface: Lesotho is dreadfully hot, so hot that fires break out.
explanation.walkthrough: H inside LESOTHO, then everything is rearranged. 'Fire' means discharging a gun or charge, not flames.
explanation.definitionFit: A shothole is a hole bored to take a blasting charge, or one made by a shot, so firing passes through it.

clue.text: One doing e.g. marquetry I nearly sacked

indicators.note: sacked as in a city plundered and wrecked, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: the seven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A craftsman confesses to almost getting fired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nearly' looks like it means removing a letter, but the whole phrase is anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Marquetry is decorative veneer inlay, so a craftsman who sets such pieces into wood is an inlayer.

clue.text: Declamation in German, one involved in conveyancing

indicators.note: in places the speech inside the abbreviation for the nationality

parts.note: Ger. is the abbreviation for German
a rant is a loud declaiming speech

explanation.surface: A German delivers a loud tirade, being caught up in a property sale.
explanation.walkthrough: G(RANT)ER.
explanation.definitionFit: In law a granter, or grantor, is the party who conveys property to another by deed.

clue.text: Hearing formerly in anteroom (less loud initially)

indicators.note: less means minus, and loud initially points to its musical abbreviation at the front

parts.note: a foyer is an entrance hall or anteroom

explanation.surface: An old courtroom hearing held in the waiting area, voices kept down.
explanation.walkthrough: FOYER minus F, the musical abbreviation forte meaning loud.
explanation.definitionFit: Oyer is an old legal term for a hearing or trial, as in oyer and terminer.

clue.text: Significant number could part with cars when getting about (13, two words)

indicators.note: getting about means moving around, so these letters travel into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written for jumbling
taken as written for jumbling

explanation.surface: An important figure might give up their cars when travelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Significant number' looks like an important person, but it is a number that signifies something in vector maths.
explanation.definitionFit: A scalar product is the single number got from multiplying two vectors, the dot product.

clue.text: Bardic ode, boring thing — departs in the course of it

indicators.note: in the course of something means partway through it, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: an awl is a tool for boring holes
d. is the timetable abbreviation for departs

explanation.surface: A tedious poem, from which people walk out partway.
explanation.walkthrough: A(D)WL. 'Boring' suggests dull, but it means drilling.
explanation.definitionFit: An awdl is a long Welsh ode in strict metre, the kind composed by bards at the Eisteddfod.

clue.text: Within the bounds of what's OK? Girl's fey about it

definitions.text: Within the bounds of what's OK

indicators.note: the girl's name is the second word wrapped about the solution, so stripping that wrapper leaves what we want

parts.note: a girl's name
taken as written: these letters sit around the rest

explanation.surface: Is it all right? The young woman is a bit otherworldly about it.
explanation.walkthrough: Read it as 'the girl is F-E-Y around it', where 'it' is the answer itself: strip those three outer letters from her name.
explanation.definitionFit: Licit means lawful or permitted, so within the limits of what is allowed.

clue.text: US cheers welcoming elected cardinal formerly?

indicators.note: welcoming means taking someone in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: later is American slang for goodbye, as cheers is in Britain
a candidate who is elected is in

explanation.surface: Americans say goodbye as they welcome a newly elected cardinal.
explanation.walkthrough: LAT(IN)ER. The question mark admits the definition is by example: a cardinal of old would know Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latiner is an old word for a Latin speaker or scholar, which a churchman like a cardinal would have been.

clue.text: Ribbon-like US or eastern bream, catch brought back

indicators.note: brought back means returned the way it came, so the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for eastern
tai is a Japanese sea bream
to net is to catch

explanation.surface: A ribbon-like fish from America or Asia, caught and hauled back in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'US' marks the American spelling, without the A of British taeniate.
explanation.definitionFit: Teniate means shaped like a tapeworm or ribbon, from Latin taenia, a band.

clue.text: Part of GCSE redone, ploughed earlier

indicators.note: part of tells us the answer is a run of letters lying within the following words

parts.note: the run of letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: A section of a school exam has been resat, as was done before.
explanation.walkthrough: GCSE is the British exam taken at about 16. Ere, or ear, is an archaic verb meaning to plough.
explanation.definitionFit: Ered is the archaic past tense of ere or ear, the old verb for tilling soil.

clue.text: Weed no longer covering lake — duck revealed

indicators.note: in a down clue covering means sitting on top, so this piece comes first

parts.note: tea was old slang for marijuana, now dated
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Pondweed has cleared from a lake, revealing a duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Covering' looks like a container, but here one piece sits above the other.
explanation.definitionFit: The teal is a small freshwater dabbling duck.

clue.text: Name of old characters regularly omitted in interment

indicators.note: dropping letters at regular intervals leaves every second one standing

parts.note: the even letters of the word

explanation.surface: An ancient name, with some letters lost from a burial inscription.
explanation.walkthrough: Nemn is a Spenserian word in Chambers.
explanation.definitionFit: Nemn is an obsolete verb meaning to name, used by Spenser.

clue.text: Spirits without a dash of soda — can you keep it under your hat?

definitions.text: can you keep it under your hat?

indicators.note: without means lacking, so that letter comes off

parts.note: the manes were the spirits of the dead in Roman religion

indicators.note: a dash is a small splash, so just the opening letter is wanted

parts.note: its initial letter

explanation.surface: Drinking spirits neat, without soda, is a secret you might keep to yourself.
explanation.walkthrough: Spirits are not drinks but Roman ghosts. 'Keep it under your hat' looks like keeping a secret; literally, long hair stays under the hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A mane is a long thick head of hair, which a person can tuck under a hat.

clue.text: Drag act's last, daring though with less removed)

indicators.note: removed tells us to cut out the named letters from the bold word
last points to the final letter of the word before it

parts.note: its final letter
reckless means rashly daring

explanation.surface: A drag act finishes; it was bold, though less so with something cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drag act' looks like cross-dressing, but drag is the definition. Treck is a variant of trek, to haul.
explanation.definitionFit: Treck is an old variant of trek, meaning to drag or haul, as oxen pulled a wagon.

clue.text: Tramp, a long time in garment

indicators.note: in places the long period inside the clothing

parts.note: a tog is a garment, as in togs
an era is a long age

explanation.surface: A vagrant wearing the same clothes for ages.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is British slang; it originally meant a tramp, from the rags wrapped round the feet in place of socks.
explanation.definitionFit: A toerag was a vagrant or tramp, a word now used as a general insult for a scoundrel.

clue.text: Live sac, active, may be this

definitions.text: Live sac, active, may be this

indicators.note: active means busy and moving, so the letters are set in motion into a new order

parts.note: the seven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An active living sac could be described with this word.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: a live, active sac such as the bladder is vesical.
explanation.definitionFit: Vesical means relating to a bladder, a sac in the body, especially the urinary one.

clue.text: Even bits of deal chaps put together, like many old coffins?

indicators.note: even bits are those in second and fourth places, so only those letters are kept

parts.note: its second and fourth letters
chaps are men

explanation.surface: Planks of cheap wood joined by workmen, as for coffins of old.
explanation.walkthrough: Deal looks like the pine timber, fitting coffins, but it only supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Elmen means made of elm wood, the traditional timber for coffins.

clue.text: Nuns taken round new Church in carriages

indicators.note: to be taken round something is to enclose it, so the nuns wrap the rest

parts.note: Poor Clares are an order of nuns
N is the abbreviation for new
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Nuns take a new church on a tour by horse-drawn coach.
explanation.walkthrough: CLARE(N CE)S.
explanation.definitionFit: A clarence was a closed four-wheeled horse-drawn carriage, named after the Duke of Clarence.
